column3: Show or renew network adapter settings; ipconfig /all includes DNS and DHCP lease details.
Create, start, stop or query Windows services from the command line.
Schedule a task to run at a given time or on logon; /create, /run and /delete manage entries.
Read or edit the Windows registry from the console (reg query, reg add, reg delete).
Robust directory copier; /MIR mirrors a source tree including deletions.
Scan and repair protected Windows system files with /scannow.
Servicing tool for Windows images and the component store (no tldr page at the pinned path; expect a skip).
Configure network interfaces, firewall rules and proxy settings; netsh winsock reset rebuilds the Winsock catalog.
Display or change NTFS access control lists (grant, deny, reset).
List running processes with PIDs, memory usage and the services backing each one.
Control power plans and sleep states; powercfg /lastwake reports the last wake source.
Install, upgrade and uninstall packages from the Windows package manager.
End a process by PID or image name; /f forces termination.
Open a Windows command interpreter or run a single command string with /c.
List files and subdirectories in a folder with sizes and dates.
Show or change the current working directory of the shell.
Copy one or more files to another location within the same volume.
Delete one or more files; wildcards select groups of files.
Print text to the console, useful in batch scripts and for @echo off toggling.
Search files for regular-expression or literal string patterns.
Run a command against each selected file, e.g. files older than N days.
Format a drive or volume with a chosen file system.
Show the media access control address of each network adapter.
Print the name of the current Windows computer.
Create a symbolic or hard link to a file or directory (needs /d for directory links).
Display file or piped input one screen at a time.
Move files or rename a directory.
Show active TCP connections, listening ports and the owning process.
Query DNS servers for host name or address records.
Trace the route to a host and measure per-hop packet loss over time.
Test reachability and round-trip latency of a host with ICMP echo packets.
Remove an empty directory, or /s /q to delete a tree without confirmation.
Rename one or more files without moving them.
Show or modify the local IP routing table (route print, route add).
Start a program under a different user account than the logged-on one.
Schedule or cancel a shutdown, reboot or sign-out of the machine.
Report machine-level facts: OS build, install date, RAM, hotfixes and network card.
List the routers packets cross on the way to a destination (traceroute).
Print an indented tree of a directory and its subdirectories.
Print the contents of a text file to standard output.
Locate which path entry a command file is resolved from.
Print the user (and group membership) the shell is running as.
Query the WMI instrumentation layer for system and configuration facts.
Show or change file attributes such as hidden, read-only and system.
Manage background file transfers through the BITS job queue.
Dump, create or verify certificate stores and file hashes from the console.
Check a disk for file-system errors and repair them with /f or scan with /scan.
Encrypt folders with EFS or wipe free space so deleted data can no longer be recovered.
Copy console or piped input onto the Windows clipboard.
Clear the console screen buffer.
Partition and manage disks from an interactive scripting shell.
Recall and edit command lines, and record macros for the console session.
List installed device drivers with their state and start mode.
Extract files from a cabinet archive (.cab).
Compare two files or sets of files and show the differing lines.
Print lines of a file that contain a given string (exact literal match).
Run a command once for each item in a file, directory or string list.
Show or change which program opens each file extension class.
Dump the group policy objects and settings that applied at sign-in.
List the built-in cmd.exe commands and show help text for one.
Create, change or delete the volume label of a drive.
Send a message to a user, session or session id on the machine.
Save the current directory on a stack and change to a new one (popd returns).
Set a user or system environment variable that persists across sessions.
Sort lines of piped or file input alphabetically, with /r to reverse.
Assign ownership of a file or directory to the administrator group.
Copy files and directory trees with attribute and permission preservation.
List directory contents with sizes, hidden files (ls -la) and human-readable units (ls -lh).
Copy files and directories; cp -r recurses into trees, cp -a preserves attributes.
Move or rename files and directories; mv -f overwrites without prompting.
Remove files or, with rm -rf, a directory tree irreversibly.
Print or concatenate files to standard output.
Change file permission bits numerically (chmod 755) or symbolically (chmod +x).
Change the owning user and group of a file or directory.
Start an OpenSSH client session or run a remote command on another host.
Report file-system disk usage per mounted volume (df -h for human units).
Estimate disk usage of files and directory trees (du -sh sums a directory).
Select lines matching a regular expression; grep -r recurses, -c counts matches.
Create or extract archives; compress or extract with tar -czf / tar -xzf (.tar.gz) or -J for .xz.
Transfer data to or from a URL; -O saves the remote filename, -o names it yourself.
Search a directory tree for files by name, size, age and run actions on the hits.
Print the first lines of each input file (head -n 20).
Print the last lines of a file; tail -f follows growth, as on log files.
Sort lines of text alphabetically (-r reverses, -n compares numerically).
Filter repeated, adjacent lines and with -c count occurrences of each.
Count lines, words and bytes of input (wc -l for line counts).
Pattern-scanning language for column-split text processing and reports.
Stream editor for find-and-replace and line-range edits (sed s/a/b/g).
Translate, squeeze or delete characters from standard input.
Build and run command lines from standard input, e.g. piping find output into rm.
Create hard links or, with -s, symbolic links between files.
Create one or more new directories (mkdir -p creates intermediate levels).
Compare two files line by line; diff -u shows a unified context patch.
Detect the file type of each argument from content, not extension.
Show used and available physical and swap memory (free -h for human units).
Pager for viewing file or pipe output one screen at a time, with search.
Locate a command by searching PATH and printing the first hit.
Print the effective user name of the current process.
Send a signal to a process by pid; kill -9 forces termination.
Snapshot running processes (ps aux for every process on the system).
Interactive view of processes sorted by CPU and memory, refreshed in place.
Pause execution for a given number of seconds; used inside scripts and loops.
Print kernel name, release and architecture (uname -a shows everything).
Print or set the system date and time in a chosen format.
Run a command in a modified environment or print current variables.
Show the manual page of a command, function or config file format.
Read standard input and write it to both a file and standard output.
Send ICMP ECHO_REQUEST packets to a host and report round-trip times.
Compress or decompress a file with standards-mode DEFLATE compression.
Simple terminal text editor with visible key hints at the bottom bar.
Synchronize files and directory trees across machines or paths, copying only the deltas.
Copy files over an SSH connection to or from a remote host.
Convert and copy a file byte by byte; used for raw disk image writes.
Control the systemd service manager: start, stop, enable, disable and status of units.
Query the systemd journal, filtered by unit, priority or time window.
Show and manage addresses, routes and links; ip a is the modern ifconfig replacement.
Debian/Ubuntu package manager front end: apt install, update, upgrade.
Low-level APT client with scriptable install, download and dependency handling.
Debian package file tool: dpkg -i installs, -r removes, -l lists what is registered.
Schedule recurring user jobs; crontab -e edits the table, -l lists it.
Create a new login account on the system.
Delete a login account and, with -r, its home directory.
Modify an existing user account, e.g. group membership with -aG.
Create a new system group definition.
Query or change the system host name and related machine settings.
Show or set system clock, time zone and NTP synchronization.
Attach a file system or image to a directory in the tree.
Detach a mounted file system once no process holds it open.
Configure or display network interfaces (legacy tool, superseded by ip).
Run a System V init script or request the systemd unit status of a service.
Schedule a machine shutdown or reboot; shutdown -h now stops immediately.
Change a user's default login shell.
Change a user's login password.
List open files, sockets and the processes holding them (lsof -i :port).
